title: CBC and Red Cell Indices: MCV, MCH, MCHC and RDW
summary: How red cell indices classify anemias and how to correlate them with the peripheral smear.
objectives: Classify anemias using MCV and MCHC.
Explain what RDW adds to the classification.

highYield: MCV < 80 fL = microcytic; MCV > 100 fL = macrocytic.
MCHC low = hypochromic (e.g., iron deficiency); MCHC high is seen in hereditary spherocytosis.
High RDW = mixed or developing population (e.g., iron deficiency); normal RDW in thalassemia trait.

deepStudy.introduction: Red cell indices are calculated from the CBC: MCV = Hct/RBC, MCH = Hb/RBC, MCHC = Hb/Hct. They screen for the mechanism of anemia before the smear confirms morphology.

sections.heading: Index calculations
sections.body: All indices are mathematically derived from hemoglobin, hematocrit and red cell count measured by the automated analyzer. Artifacts (cold agglutinins, hyperglycemia, high WBC) can falsely raise MCV and MCHC.

sections.heading: RDW in classification
sections.body: RDW measures red cell size distribution. Iron deficiency typically shows high RDW early; thalassemia trait shows microcytosis with a normal RDW. A normal RDW with low MCV points toward thalassemia trait.

deepStudy.clinicalSignificance: Index-based classification directs the next lab tests: ferritin and iron studies vs hemoglobin electrophoresis vs B12/folate.
deepStudy.labInterpretation: Indices are screening tools; confirm with smear review and specific assays. Reference intervals vary per analyzer and population.
examTraps: Cold agglutinins falsely elevate MCV and MCHC — warm the sample and re-run.
A normal MCV does not exclude early iron deficiency (check RDW and ferritin).
